Ballot Measure Rebuttal Argument Submission Form
If both an argument in favor of and an argument against a measure have been selected for publication in the Sample
Ballot & Official Voter Information Pamphlet, a typed rebuttal to the argument in favor of or the argument against the
measure may be submitted as outlined in this form.
The author(s) of the primary argument of the measure may prepare and submit a rebuttal argument or may authorize
in writing any other person or persons to prepare, submit or sign the rebuttal argument.
A rebuttal argument will not be accepted unless accompanied by this completed form, which shall contain the printed
name(s) and signature(s) of the person(s) submitting it or, if submitted on behalf of a bona fide association of citizens,
the name of the association and the printed name and signature of at least one of its principal officers. Please make
sure you are using proper format before submitting to the Elections Office.
Word count limit for Rebuttal Arguments = 250 words

Vote NO on Measure DD — Protect Public Safety and Nonprofit Funding
Supporters of Measure DD cite "fireworks-related" incidents, but they do not tell you how many
involved legal, State Fire Marshal-approved Safe and Sane fireworks and how many involved
illegal aerial fireworks and explosives. That distinction matters.
Recent City reports show that fireworks-related calls and citations have substantially declined.
Police Chief Matt Lethin has stated that the decrease is significant enough that the department
expects to use a reduced operational approach in future years.
That progress shows that education, prevention, and enforcement efforts are working.
San Bruno's nonprofit organizations have sold legal fireworks to fund services to our community
for decades while also helping fund Fourth of July public safety efforts.
The legal fireworks program helps support police services, fire prevention, public education,
inspections, enforcement, and cleanup. Measure DD would eliminate that funding.
It would also eliminate an important source of support for local youth sports, veterans' programs,
scholarships, camps, school activities, community projects, and families in need. With no
replacement for this funding or these programs.
If Measure DD passes, illegal fireworks will remain illegal and enforcement will still be
necessary. But the nonprofit funding that supports community programs and helps offset public
safety costs will disappear.
Don't mistake banning something legal for solving the problem of illegal fireworks.
Protect San Bruno's nonprofits and public safety. Focus enforcement where it belongs: on
illegal fireworks. Vote NO on Measure DD.
End
